Title: France's Safran pumps €136mil into Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: French aerospace group Safran Landing Systems is investing €136 million (about RM640 million) to expand its manufacturing facility in Sendayan and open a new carbon brake maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) centre in Nilai, both in Negri Sembilan.
The investments comprise €134 million for the expansion of its Sendayan facility and €2 million for the new MRO centre, which will serve about 100 airline operators across Asia Pacific.
The expanded facilities will support aircraft operated by airlines using Airbus A320, A321 and A350, Boeing 737, 777 and 787, as well as ATR aircraft.
The Sendayan expansion adds 7,000 square metres of manufacturing space, including a new textile production line, carbonisation furnaces and advanced machining equipment.
The facility, which currently employs 160 people, is expected to double its carbon brake disc production capacity by 2028.
The new 1,000-square-metre MRO centre in Nilai is located near Kuala Lumpur International Airport and about 20km from the Sendayan plant, which will supply it with new and refurbished carbon brake discs.
Safran Landing Systems chief executive officer François Bastin said the investments reflected Malaysia's strategic role in the group's global industrial operations and its commitment to supporting the region's aviation growth.
The company plans to increase its Malaysian workforce to 220 employees by 2030 across its manufacturing and MRO operations, strengthening local expertise in aerospace manufacturing and maintenance services.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority chief executive officer Datuk Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim Sikh Abdul Majid said the investments reflected Safran's confidence in Malaysia's aerospace industry.
He said the expansion would create long-term economic value, support high-skilled employment and strengthen the country's aerospace capabilities.
Safran has operated in Malaysia for more than 50 years, with its activities evolving from supply and servicing into manufacturing and now, MRO operations.
On sustainability, Safran said its Sendayan facility reduced greenhouse gas emissions by 60 per cent between 2018 and 2025 through the use of lower-carbon local energy sources and the recovery of process gases.
Additional sustainable energy capacity is planned by 2030 to further reduce emissions.
The investments are part of Safran Landing Systems' broader push to strengthen its Asia Pacific presence, following the inauguration of an expanded landing gear MRO facility in Singapore in September 2026.

Title: Headmaster given 20 years' jail, rotan for pornography, sexual assault of student, 12
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A headmaster was sentenced to 20 years' jail and 11 strokes of the rotan after the Court of Appeal found him guilty of producing child pornography and sexual assault of a 12-year-old student five years ago.
The three-member panel of judges led by Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, sitting with Datuk Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, denied the final appeal of Anuar Kintan for producing child pornography.
The court also allowed the prosecution's appeal of the 59-year-old's acquittal on the sexual assault charge which had been delivered by a lower court.
On the first charge, the court affirmed the sentence of nine years' jail and eight strokes of the rotan which had been handed down by the Ipoh High Court.
On the sexual assault charge, the appellate court sentenced Anuar to 10 years' jail and one stroke of the rotan, as well as an extra year and two strokes under Section 16(1) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
The court ordered that the jail sentences run consecutively, starting from today.
Anuar was also ordered to be placed under police supervision for two years after his release from prison.
Anuar had been charged with producing child pornography by taking pictures of the victim at a primary school in Perak about 10am on April 3, 2021.
The charge was framed under Section 5 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act, read together with Section 16(1) of the same.
Delivering the court's judgment, Noorin the testimony of the victim, referred to as the fourth prosecution witness (SP4), the photographs found, and the results of a forensic examination of the accused's mobile phone supported the conviction.
"SP4 identified Anuar as the person who took the pictures, while the pictures marked as P11A and P11B shows the victim's body.
"Forensic analysis confirmed that the images were in the accused's phone," she said.
She said the defence contended that the pictures could have been sent to the accused by someone else or that the phone was accessible to other people.
"However, the court is of the view that merely suggesting an alternative explanation does not necessarily raise reasonable doubt when the evidence is assessed as a whole.
"The court also finds that the alibi the defence presented was insufficiently substantiated to overturn the findings of the lower court," she said.
On the second charge, Anuar was accused of committing sexual assault on the girl at the school at the same time and date.
Noorin said the lower court had acquitted and discharged the accused after accepting his alibi, including the testimony of his wife, the seventh defence witness (SD7), who claimed that they were at home at the time.
"However, the court found that the testimony of another friend of the victim (SP5), who accompanied the victim to school on the morning of the incident, materially supported the prosecution's case," she said.
She said SP5 had testified that they arrived in school at 9.30am and then went to the headmaster's office.
"SP5 later saw the victim and the accused leaving the office together. About half an hour later, the victim returned (to SP5) and they left the school.
"While on their way home, the victim told SP5 that the accused had touched her body," she said.
Noorin said the court stressed that the burden of proof remained with the prosecution throughout, and that the decision to convict the accused was made after assessing all the evidence, including SP4's testimony, which was materially corroborated by SP5's observations.
"The court was satisfied that the prosecution had proved the second charge beyond reasonable doubt," she said.
However, the appellate court dismissed the prosecution's appeal against two other charges of sexual assault, affirming the High Court's acquittal of Anuar on those counts.
Prosecution was handled by deputy public prosecutor Azlina Mahmod while Anuar was represented by Amir Khusyairi Mohamad Tanusi.

Title: MCA accepts two seats for Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MCA has accepted the two seats allocated to it by Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka state election.
Its president, Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong, said the decision was made after receiving assurances that the party's role in representing the Chinese community in Melaka would not be sidelined.
He said discussions among BN component parties had yielded positive results, with BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi responding positively to issues raised by MCA.
"We have been assured that the representation of the Chinese community, especially MCA will not be sidelined and continue to play a role.
"Zahid has also assured us that Chinese participation in the state government will not be sidelined and that we will work together to uphold BN's aspirations," he told a press conference after chairing the MCA Presidential Council meeting here today.
Wee said the focus now was on coordinating election efforts to secure victory and form a strong, balanced state government.

Title: Iran to woo M'sian tourists with historical and cultural attractions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Iran and Malaysia are developing practical programmes in cultural and halal tourism, heritage protection and handicrafts.
Iran's Deputy Minister of Cultural Heritage, Tourism and Handicrafts Ali Darabi, shared this in an exclusive interview with IRNA, according to TV BRICS.
The two countries are working to expand tourist and cultural exchanges, as well as participation in tourism events and exhibitions, Darabi said, after meeting Malaysia's Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing on the sidelines of the fourth session of the Asian Cultural Heritage Alliance in Hangzhou, China.
According to the official, protecting cultural heritage requires international cooperation in technical knowledge exchange, joint training and restoration based on scientific methods and recognised standards.
Iran also seeks to attract more Malaysian tourists by promoting the country's historical, cultural and natural attractions, it reported.
Darabi called for closer cooperation between travel and tourism companies and agencies in the two countries.
He also proposes holding an "Iran Week" in Malaysia to showcase Iran's cultural and civilisational heritage.

Title: PN seeks contempt proceedings against RoS over registration revocation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional has applied to the High Court for permission to initiate committal proceedings against the Registrar of Societies (RoS) over the revocation of its registration.
PN claimed the move amounted to contempt of court as it was made before its application for a stay of the decision was heard.
The application was filed by PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and four other party leaders, naming Registrar of Societies Datuk Mohd Zulfikar Ahmad as the respondent.
Lawyer Rafique Rashid Ali confirmed that the application was filed yesterday.
He said case management was scheduled in chambers on Nov 12.

Title: E-Commerce Bill to include licensing rules – Armizan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The E-Commerce Bill, aimed at strengthening accountability among online platforms and sellers, is being revised to include a licensing regime.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Seri Armizan Mohd Ali said the ministry was ready to table the bill earlier, but the cabinet called for further improvements.
"When we took the bill to the cabinet, it asked for several improvements, including a firm licensing regime.
"That is why we had to revise it. I apologise, and we will expedite it," he said in response to Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar) in the Dewan Rakyat.
Armizan said he received repeated instructions to speed up the bill's tabling and had sought assistance from other ministries and the Attorney-General's Chambers.
Earlier, Syed Saddiq said Shopee and TikTok Shop had raised their platform fees more than 10 times since the bill was announced in 2023, with fees now reaching up to 25 per cent.
He urged the government to expedite the bill, warning that small traders could otherwise be driven out of business.
Armizan said the bill would focus on four key areas.

Title: Perlis considers removing jetty wall after MMEA sailor killed
Article:
ARAU: The Perlis government will consider removing the concrete wall of an old jetty in Sungai Padang after a Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) patrol boat struck it two days ago.
The crash threw four sailors overboard, killing one.
Speaking after the groundbreaking ceremony for the Sanglang Port, Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah said the state would assess whether the wall should remain.
He added that the state government would finalise assistance for the widow and family of 41-year-old Leading Seaman (Technical) Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan.
"Tonight we will decide how much assistance the state government can channel to the widow and the family of the deceased," he said.
In the 11.30pm incident on Monday, the patrol boat, carrying five personnel, crashed into the wall while pursuing a boat suspected of carrying illegal immigrants.
Roshaimi was killed after being thrown into the sea and is believed to have struck his head against the concrete wall.
Three other
personnel were injured,
including one who suffered a broken right arm.

Title: Zahid signals unity amid BN-MCA seat dispute
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has sought to reassure the coalition's members amid a dispute with MCA over seat allocations for the Melaka election.
In a Facebook post, Zahid shared an image of himself clasping hands with MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong, with BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir standing beside them.
"Don't worry. All is well. We are the 'Blue Gang'," he wrote.
Zahid, who is also Umno president, did not elaborate on the status of negotiations over MCA's seats or candidates.
The New Straits Times has reached out to Wee for comment.
Yesterday, Zahid said
seat talks
with MCA had ended positively, leaving Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to announce the outcome. The discussions involved Wee, Zambry and Ab Rauf.
Wee, however, said it was
premature
to describe the talks as positive, as both sides remained some distance from an agreement.
The dispute came to the fore when
Wee walked out
during the introduction of BN's candidates at the Melaka International Trade Centre over dissatisfaction with seat negotiations.
He said he had left to defend MCA's dignity and rights as a BN component party.
Wee also said he remained unsure whether MCA would contest the upcoming Melaka election, adding that the party would assess the progress of negotiations.

Melaka polls amid seat talks, says Wee

Title: States without sufficient water supply cannot host data centres, says Johari
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: States without sufficient water supply will not be allowed to host data centres, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
"If a state does not have enough water, it must not be a host for data centres," he said when winding up the debate on the 2027 Supply bill today.
Johari (BN-Titiwangsa) said the government said the government would consult state governments before approving data centre projects.
"If a state does not have sufficient water supply, even if it has space (for data centres), we cannot give it (approval).
"That is why we will check with the state government," he said.
He said investors were also encouraged to introduce water recycling technology, allowing Malaysia to benefit from their expertise.
Johari added that states should charge data centres higher water rates than ordinary users.
He was responding to Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam), who asked who determined the energy and water supply for data centres.
Johari said applications had to be submitted through the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida), which also considered input from the Data Centre Task Force (DCTF).
The task force comprises the Investment, Trade and Industry, Digital, and Energy Transition and Water Transformation ministries.
He said electricity would be supplied to data centres only when there was sufficient surplus capacity and an adequate reserve margin.
"If there is no surplus, we do it off-grid," he said.
Malaysia has approved 117 data centres, of which 55 are operating, 19 are under construction and 16 have yet to begin construction. Another 27 are at various stages of development and will obtain electricity through off-grid arrangements, he said.
If all 117 projects are completed, they will require an estimated 23,000 to 23,500 megawatts (MW) of electricity, he added.
Johari said electricity supplied to data centres would not be subsidised and would be priced according to world market rates.
He said the growth of data centres could also create an opportunity for Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), the world's fifth-largest gas exporter, to sell natural gas at market prices without long-term agreements.
"For exports, we usually sign long-term agreements with countries abroad.
"But if we have data centres, with their power built separately from existing industries, we may be able to use this gas at market price without signing long-term agreements, because the data centre is already in Malaysia," he said.

Title: Motorcyclist riding against traffic killed in head-on crash with MPV
Article:
MARAN: A motorcyclist was killed after riding against traffic and colliding head-on with a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) at Km 59 of Jalan Kuantan-Kuala Lumpur yesterday.
Md Yusoff Daud, 75, was riding alone when the accident occurred about 4pm.
Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said the accident involved a Honda Wave motorcycle and a Toyota Vellfire.
"The Toyota driver was travelling from Kuantan towards Sri Jaya when a motorcyclist riding against the flow of traffic collided with his vehicle.
"The motorcyclist died at the scene due to severe injuries, while the Toyota driver was unhurt," he said in a statement.
A one-minute dashcam video of the incident, recorded by the Toyota driver which has gone viral, showed the vehicle negotiating a bend before colliding with the oncoming motorcyclist, who was flung onto the road.
Wong said the case was still under investigation and urged witnesses to contact the investigating officer, Inspector Muhaimin Omar, at 017-9436741.

Title: NRES to propose drought action plan to National Disaster Management Council - Arthur
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) will propose the development of a drought action plan to the National Disaster Management Council to strengthen preparedness for the phenomenon.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the proposal would be submitted for the council's consideration, so that action plans for floods and droughts could also be developed, in addition to the existing National Haze Action Plan.
"This is something that will be brought to the National Disaster Management Council, so that, apart from an action plan for haze, we will also have action plans for floods and droughts," he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Datuk Mumtaz Md Nawi (PN-Tumpat) on the government's measures in the event of a severe drought or El Nino, including identifying high-risk areas and coordinating efforts among departments, while winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027) at the policy stage, for his ministry.
Earlier, Arthur said that, based on current projections, the strong El Nino phenomenon was expected to intensify to the very strong category between November 2026 and January 2027, and could persist until May 2027.
He added that the phenomenon could bring drier weather and extreme heat between January and May 2027, with maximum temperatures potentially reaching 40 degrees Celsius, particularly in the northern and interior parts of the Peninsula, as well as several interior areas of Sabah and Sarawak.
He said reduced rainfall was also expected, particularly between January and March 2027, with potentially more significant effects in the northern part of the Peninsula and Sabah.
In another development, Arthur said the implementation of a carbon tax should be carried out carefully and in stages, once the Climate Change Bill and the Climate Change Authority Bill were passed and gazetted, and their implementation frameworks were operating effectively.
Industry readiness must be taken into account to ensure that the transition to a low-carbon economy would not affect the country's economic growth.
"NRES continues to provide cooperation and technical input to the Finance Ministry, to ensure that the implementation of any carbon pricing instruments is in line with the country's climate change policies and commitments," he said.
Meanwhile, on the issue of transboundary haze, he said that the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP) did not currently provide for a specific mechanism for compensation claims between countries.
However, Arthur said the government was open to examining the suitability of other legal mechanisms for compensation and damages, subject to the availability of a legal basis under international law.
"In this regard, a comprehensive study of the economic losses caused by haze, including its effects on public health, productivity and economic activity, is important as a scientific and economic basis for policy consideration and follow-up action," he said.
Proposals for financial assistance to affected people, particularly gig workers, and the establishment of a haze disaster fund, required further study with the relevant ministries and agencies, taking into account existing assistance mechanisms, actual needs and the government's financial implications.
The government would also continue to strengthen enforcement cooperation through bilateral and Asean channels, including by promoting the implementation of the polluter pays principle, he said.

Title: Boustead Plantations sale tests LTAT's priorities in protecting contributors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The proposed sale of a controlling stake in Boustead Plantations Bhd (BPlant) has put the Armed Forces Fund Board's (LTAT) choice of buyer under scrutiny, challenging it to secure the best value while safeguarding contributors' long-term interests.
SD Guthrie Bhd, Tradewinds Plantation Bhd and Achi Jaya Plantations Sdn Bhd have been reported as contenders for the plantation business.
Their proposals require LTAT to weigh sale proceeds alongside each buyer's financial capacity, operational experience and commitment to developing the estates.
The differences between competing offers are understood to range from about RM300 million to RM800 million, depending on the proposals being compared and their respective terms.
An industry observer said that if the disposal was intended to reduce LTAT's debt, securing the best overall financial outcome should be central to the selection.
The observer said stronger sale proceeds could ease financing pressure and strengthen the fund's capacity to deliver returns to contributors.
If a lower offer is selected, the additional benefits offered must be compelling enough to justify the valuation gap.
LTAT must also clarify how these benefits will be measured, monitored and guaranteed.
The existing plantation operations of each bidder provide another basis for assessing their ability to take over BPlant's operations and finance improvements.
Available data shows that SD Guthrie's upstream landbank in Malaysia stands at about 336,575 hectares, compared with 156,138 hectares for Tradewinds' plantation landbank.
Achi Jaya is listed with 11,349 hectares in the comparison, although it remains unclear whether this figure reflects the company's entire current landbank.
The figures indicate significant differences in the documented scale of operations.
However, landbank size alone does not determine financial strength, management quality or the merits of an acquisition proposal.
Each bidder should be evaluated against criteria, including financing arrangements, estate management resources and the ability to sustain investments after the acquisition is completed.
The current sale process follows a proposal involving Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) that was not finalised three years ago.
The proposal, first submitted on Aug 24, 2023, involved KLK's offer of RM1.15 billion for a 33 per cent stake and one share at RM1.55 per share.
The offer valued BPlant at RM3.47 billion in total.
The proposed sale excluded two parcels of land in Penang and Selangor, which LTAT could separate for future property development.
The RM3.47 billion figure represented the valuation of 100 per cent of BPlant and should be distinguished from current offers for a 75 per cent stake.
Any comparison should also account for differences in the assets included in the transaction, transaction terms and BPlant's financial position.
Nevertheless, the earlier proposal provides a benchmark for examining changes in BPlant's value and the benefits targeted for LTAT.
Under the current proposed structure, LTAT will retain a minority stake.
This makes the buyer's ability to improve BPlant's performance important to future dividends and the residual value of LTAT's investment.
The evaluation of bidders should cover total investments in replanting, mill maintenance and productivity improvements.
The investment implementation timeline and available financing sources will help determine whether the proposals can deliver sustainable improvements.
LTAT's ability to enforce investment commitments is also important in protecting its interests after the sale.
The industry observer also questioned how LTAT will protect the plantation assets after the transaction is completed.
These include restrictions on land sales, future changes in land use and the rights LTAT would retain as a shareholder.
LTAT's asset management has already attracted attention in Parliament.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin explained that LTAT's leasehold interest in land in Ampang Hilir was sold to the US government for RM420 million through a tender process.
He said the disposal was part of efforts to rebalance the fund's asset portfolio, while ownership of the land remained with the Federal Lands Commissioner.
The BPlant transaction presents another test of LTAT's ability to demonstrate the financial and operational benefits of its asset-related decisions.
Clear explanations of competing offers, investment commitments and safeguards will help contributors assess whether the selected buyer delivers the best overall outcome for their savings and retirement interests.

Title: Malaysians missing in Nepal: Perkeso review, cabinet hearing soon on aid for families
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH) says eligible families of the 54 Malaysians missing in Nepal will receive immediate Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) payouts.
This follows a meeting with Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan today.
MASFIH spokesman Dr R. Manivannan said Ramanan had asked the Perkeso chief executive to immediately review the missing Malaysians' coverage under the scheme, with eligible claims to be paid out without delay.
He said Perkeso needed the identity card numbers of the missing, which the families had not previously collected.
"So, I've committed to collect as much as possible by today and give it to them before the end of the day, and they've committed to process whatever is available, and what is not will be handled tomorrow," he said.
Manivannan said the families had agreed to sign a letter of indemnity to protect the ministry and the minister from any backlash.
Under it, he said, the family members will return the money should their missing family members come home.
"I think that is a fair arrangement. At least immediately it will help those families who are eligible to be covered under Perkeso," he said.
Manivannan said Ramanan would also bring MASFIH's request for one-off humanitarian aid for all 54 families to the cabinet meeting this Friday.
"And he was quite assuring that it will be given. Even if it's not, he will do the necessary," he said.
The group had earlier called on the government to
provide humanitarian aid
to the families, and to appoint Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan to coordinate assistance.
The aid, said Manivannan, would help cover household expenses and other essential commitments while the families waited for answers.
"For these families, timely financial assistance would provide a meaningful relief during an exceptionally difficult period.
"It will not resolve the uncertainty surrounding the missing loved ones, but it will ease some of the practical and financial pressures they face while continuing to wait and hope," he told reporters.
The 54 Malaysians have been missing for 64 days since a flash flood struck Rasuwagadhi, along the Nepal-Tibet border, on Aug 26.
Meanwhile, Manivannan said Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (Mitra) director-general Ravindran Nair had also been appointed to help the families deal with other agencies and push through outstanding matters, even though the group also included Malay and Chinese families.

Title: MyCC proposes action against 18 enterprises over RM108.3mil bid rigging
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) has proposed action against 18 enterprises over bid-rigging in 30 public tenders worth RM108.3 million.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the tenders involved food supplies, including for schools and public universities, as well as cleaning services.
"The tenders were issued by 12 public sector entities, comprising six ministries, three public universities, two state Islamic religious departments and one statutory body," he told the Dewan Rakyat while winding up the debate on the 2027 Supply Bill.
Armizan said evidence gathered by MyCC included centralised coordination and preparation of tender documents, the exchange of information such as proposed bid prices, and the sharing of finances and manpower among the enterprises involved.
He said the enterprises were allowed to make representations to MyCC.
"Final decision will be issued after considering the representations made by these enterprises, together with the evidence obtained during the investigation," he said.
Armizan said MyCC had also taken enforcement action against 58 companies over bid rigging, involving total penalties of RM98.49 million.
He said this covers both proposed and final decisions.
He added that MyCC was also investigating 510 companies suspected of similar activities in public and private sector tenders worth more than RM3 billion.

Title: 'You are a liar!' US-Cuba shouting match erupts at UN
Article:
UNITED NATIONS: A furious shouting match between representatives of the United States and Cuba prompted the temporary suspension of debate at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday.
The row broke out during debate on a resolution calling for an end to the US embargo on its communist-led neighbour, a non-binding measure which Cuba has put forward every year since 1992.
The debate this year, however, is taking place amid a major new pressure campaign by Washington against Cuba, including an oil blockade and broad sanctions that have severely crippled Cuba's economy.
As US Ambassador Mike Waltz was addressing the General Assembly, Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez objected to the remarks and walked up to the podium, demanding that the speech be halted.
Waltz, while arguing for the resolution to be rejected, had been criticizing repression of Cuban citizens by the communist government.
"This is the United Nations. This isn't your communist dictatorship. You cannot silence me," Waltz shouted, demanding that Rodriguez and other Cuban diplomats back away.
"You are a liar!" Rodriguez shouted back.
The chair briefly suspended the session and instructed both countries' representatives to return to their places, after which Waltz was allowed to continue.
Cuba has accused Washington of launching an "unprecedented" pressure campaign this year to persuade countries to oppose the resolution, which has traditionally had overwhelming backing.
Last year, the resolution received 165 votes in favour, seven against and 12 abstentions, its weakest level of support in two decades.
A vote on this year's resolution is expected sometime Wednesday.
The row also comes days after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Cubans to discreetly work with the CIA to end the island's communist government.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Cruise for life' dream ends with 200 passengers stranded in Cambodia
Article:
SIHANOUKVILLE: Around 200 passengers who paid to live on a cruise ship while travelling the world were abruptly left in a Cambodian port after the company ran out of money, an official said on Wednesday.
US-based operator Villa Vie Residences announced on Tuesday it had "suspended operations in Cambodia" as it worked to address "extraordinary increases" in fuel costs following the Iran war.
The 200-metre Odyssey left Northern Ireland in October 2024 for a continuous voyage for which residents could buy or rent rooms for a holiday or for life – some passengers selling everything they had to pay for it.
However, passengers were given just seven hours to pack their bags and leave during a scheduled stop in the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville, according to Long Dimanche, deputy governor of Preah Sihanouk province.
He said in a statement 203 guests and 156 crew had arrived aboard the Bahamas-flagged ship from Thailand on Oct 23, and had been due to go on to Vietnam.
"The sudden order to disembark has left many retirees and remote workers homeless thousands of miles from their home countries," he said.
Some passengers took flights out while others remained in the city, he said, adding that the ship itself was due to refuel and leave on October 31.
Randy Cassingham, a passenger on board who runs a cruise blog, wrote that the disembarkation order followed a "cascade of problems."
Under a post entitled "Abandon Ship!", he said its Belfast launch was delayed by four months, while the ship never reached its capacity of 650 residents, peaking at around 350.
He said it was not a "luxury" ship but affordable – until the company started "begging for money."
Villa Vie said in its statement per-cabin monthly fuel expenses had gone from an average of US$1,800 to an estimated US$6,000 to US$8,000 in parts of Asia.
"The company cannot simply pass increases of that scale on to residents, and the resulting shortfall has placed its current operating model under unsustainable financial pressure," it said.
Cassingham accused the company of doing "absolutely nothing to help" stranded passengers.
Villa Vie said it was "working with residents to coordinate disembarkation and identify temporary living arrangements."
"Villa Vie Residences recognises that this is a difficult and disruptive period for residents, crew members, and employees, and is working to support those affected as plans develop," it said.--AFP

Title: Maxis shares slip after reports of revived merger plans with U Mobile
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Maxis Bhd shares slipped in late trading today following reports of renewed plans for a potential merger with U Mobile Sdn Bhd, which could create the country's largest wireless operator.
At 4.30pm, Maxis shares fell 16 sen, or 4.38 per cent, to RM3.49, with 3.98 million shares traded.
According to reports, both telecommunication companies are reviving plans to combine the companies in a deal that could create the country's biggest wireless operator by market value, people with knowledge of the matter said.
The report said Maxis is moving a step closer to a merger by asking a select group of banks and law firms to submit proposals.
"The potential transaction is gaining traction as both sides are showing more willingness to negotiate," the report said.
In 2024, Maxis had an early discussion on consideration of buying out U Mobile, reports said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four charged with trafficking maid who suffered severe burns
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Four people, including a married couple, were charged at the Sessions Court today with trafficking an Indonesian domestic worker for forced labour, allegedly leaving her with severe burns.
The accused, Cheng Dee Wen and his wife, Lim Yeek Fern, both 33, Yeo Ann Sheng, 25, and R. Maneemekalai, 35, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to them before Judge Rohaida Ishak.
They were jointly charged with trafficking Siti Rohaya for forced labour exploitation through the use of force, resulting in serious injuries to the victim.
The offence was committed at a premises in Oren Business Centre between May and October this year.
The charge was framed under Section 13(a) of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code.
If convicted, they face life imprisonment or a jail term of not less than five years, as well as whipping.
Deputy public prosecutors Lee Jun Keong and Nadhirah Rahim prosecuted, while the accused were represented by lawyers Y. Anbananthan and Ng Sze Wei.
During proceedings, Lee objected to bail, citing the victim's status as an Indonesian who had worked at the couple's residence in the state before being rescued in Tanjung Sepat, Selangor.
He told the court that the 25-year-old victim had suffered burns covering 21 per cent of her body.
"Generally, burns affecting about 20 per cent of an adult's body can be categorised as serious injuries and require treatment in a hospital's intensive care unit," he said.
Lee also said two of the accused were the victim's employers and had access to her personal information, raising concerns that they could interfere with the victim or her family.
He urged the court to consider the possibility that the case could affect bilateral relations between Malaysia and Indonesia.
In seeking bail, Anbananthan said Cheng and Lim had a three-year-old son who was being cared for by Lim's mother, who had health problems and difficulty looking after the child.
He said Yeo was single, while Maneemekalai was married and earned RM2,400 a month, which was needed to support her family as her husband was unemployed.
The lawyer added that all four accused had permanent residential addresses and employment, and were prepared to comply with additional bail conditions.
After considering submissions from both parties, Rohaida dismissed the bail applications.
The court fixed Dec 18 for mention to obtain the chemistry report.
On Oct 19, six people were arrested after police rescued an
Indonesian woman
who had allegedly been abused and left with burns across her body.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From control to autonomy: Rethinking how managers lead
Article:
ORGANISATIONS understand the importance of employees who are innovative, proactive and adaptable, yet managers often retain tight control over decisions, procedures and how work is performed.
They want employees to think like entrepreneurs but expect them to behave like subordinates. How can organisations expect initiative when employees lack the authority to act on it?
The problem is not always a lack of delegation. Managers may assign responsibilities while retaining the authority to approve the decisions needed to fulfil them.
Employees are held responsible for results without sufficient discretion over how those results are achieved. In effect, responsibility is pushed down the hierarchy while decision-making power remains at the top.
This contradiction persists partly because managers fear mistakes and believe senior managers know best. Cultures that reward compliance over initiative reinforce this mindset.
In some organisations, involvement in every important decision becomes a sign of managerial importance. A manager who approves everything may appear indispensable, even when that dependence slows the organisation down.
Performance management systems can entrench the problem by penalising mistakes while rarely rewarding responsible experimentation.
When employees fear that a well-intentioned decision may be punished if it produces an imperfect outcome, caution becomes the safer career choice.
They may stop questioning established practices or taking responsibility for unfamiliar challenges. Compliance becomes rational, even when the organisation says it wants innovation.
Micromanagement slows decisions, discourages employees from offering ideas and leaves senior leaders burdened with operational matters that could be handled lower down the hierarchy.
As employees learn to wait for instructions rather than exercise their judgement, organisational agility suffers.
A costly cycle emerges managers retain control because they doubt employees' judgement, while employees have fewer opportunities to develop it.
Their dependence is then treated as evidence that they are not ready for autonomy.
The answer is not to eliminate oversight or give employees unrestricted freedom. Autonomy must operate within clear expectations and boundaries.
Managers should define the outcomes to be achieved and the constraints that matter, while allowing employees discretion over how to deliver results.
Decisions should be made at the level best placed to make them, with clear arrangements for escalation.
Employees need the skills, information and resources to make sound decisions and must understand their objectives and the consequences of their choices.
Managers must accept that employees may choose a different but reasonable approach to achieving the desired outcome.
The managerial role would therefore change. Rather than controlling every step, managers should set priorities, explain purpose, provide resources, remove obstacles and develop employees' skills and judgement.
They should offer guidance without taking over every decision, while remaining accountable for results. Their task is to enable effective performance, not prescribe every action.
Organisations must support this shift by reducing unnecessary approval layers, defining decision-making authority and training managers to coach rather than prescribe.
They should recognise initiative and responsible problem-solving, while maintaining safeguards proportionate to the risks involved.
Performance systems must distinguish reckless decisions from reasonable decisions made in good faith that do not produce the intended outcome. Otherwise, employees have little incentive to experiment, challenge assumptions or take ownership of problems.
The experience of companies such as Haier and Nucor illustrates how greater autonomy can be built into management systems.
Haier, the Chinese home-appliance manufacturer, developed its Rendanheyi model around smaller, customer-facing entrepreneurial units with greater responsibility for responding to market needs.
The approach seeks to bring employees closer to customers and align their work with creating value.
Nucor, the US steel manufacturer, provides another example. Its streamlined, decentralised structure gives division managers and their teams considerable responsibility for day-to-day operating decisions.
The company also emphasises employee responsibility and accountability, supported by performance-related compensation.
These examples do not prove that autonomy alone guarantees business success, nor should every organisation copy their structures.
They demonstrate, however, that decision-making authority can be distributed more widely while maintaining direction and accountability.
The challenge is to place decisions with thosebest positioned to make them, with appropriate support and clear accountability.
There is, however, a psychological difficulty in changing management behaviour.
Managers may support autonomy in principle but resist it in practice because delegating decisions can feel like losing authority, increase perceived risk or make their contributions less visible.
They must recognise that their value is not determined by how many decisions pass through their hands, but by how effectively the organisation makes decisions and develops its capacity to act.
A manager's effectiveness should be reflected in how confidently and competently employees make decisions within established boundaries, not in how dependent they remain on approval.
In a business environment marked by constant change, organisational agility is paramount.
Requiring approval for every decision can prevent companies from responding quickly and making full use of employees' abilities. The objective is not to eliminate hierarchy but to ensure that authority is exercised at the appropriate level.
The real test of leadership is not how tightly managers control the work of others, but how effectively they create the conditions in which others can do their best work.
* The writer holds an MBA from the University of Strathclyde, United Kingdom, awarded under the British Chevening Scholarship programme. With extensive experience in the financial markets and management education, he also served at a prominent think tank. The views expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Business Times

Title: Teenager sentenced to 120 hours of community service for iron rod assault
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 16-year-old boy with alleged links to a secret society was ordered to perform 120 hours of community service within six months after pleading guilty to assaulting two teenagers with an iron rod.
The teen, who cannot be named as he is a minor, was also ordered to attend an interactive workshop within the same period.
The National Legal Aid Foundation, which represented the boy, appealed for leniency, saying he had committed the offences after being mocked.
The foundation said the boy regretted his actions and had no intention of repeating them.
Deputy public prosecutor Amritpreet Kaur Randhawa did not object to the community service order but requested that the requirements be carried out consecutively.
Magistrate Atiqah Mohamed @ Mohamad Saim also ordered the boy's guardian to execute a six-month unsecured bond and ensure that he remained at home between 7pm and 7am, unless accompanied by a family member.
She directed that the community service and workshop requirements be completed separately.
She said the bond would only be discharged after the boy had fulfilled both requirements.
The boy had pleaded guilty to two counts of voluntarily causing hurt to victims aged 16 and 19 with an iron rod at 10.15pm on Sept 1, in front of a housing area in Lorong Ikan Emas, Cheras.
The offence under Section 324 of the Penal Code carries a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine, whipping or any two of these punishments upon conviction.
Police investigations found that the victims were assaulted by a group of seven men armed with weapons, including knives, pipes and a table leg.
Police arrested three people in connection with the incident on Sept 2 and seized an iron rod measuring about 57cm long.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: HBA: The government intention to adopt a profit-based valuation methodology  should be scrutinised
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Homeowners should not be expected to surrender properties they already own in exchange for promises of replacement homes under redevelopment schemes without adequate legal and financial safeguards.
Datuk Chang Kim Loong, the Honorary Secretary-General of the National House Buyers Association (HBA), said the proposed Urban Renewal Bill (URA) raises fundamental questions about the necessity of new legislation, the fairness of its valuation framework and the protection of homeowners whose properties could be earmarked for redevelopment.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming has said the proposed legislation would complement existing laws governing dilapidated strata buildings, with developers' projected profits factored into determining the value of replacement properties for affected homeowners.
However, Chang questioned whether projected profits offered a sound basis for valuation, given the uncertainties surrounding property development.
"A projected profit is not a financial guarantee, and a promise of a replacement home is not the same as receiving one," he told Business Times.
Chang argued that Malaysia already has an extensive legal framework governing land ownership, strata management, building safety, planning and compulsory land acquisition.
These include the Strata Titles Act 1985, Strata Management Act 2013, Street, Drainage and Building Act 1974 and Land Acquisition Act 1960, alongside the National Land Code 1965 and other planning and housing legislation.
While acknowledging that existing procedures may not make every redevelopment commercially or procedurally straightforward, he said this did not automatically justify introducing a comprehensive new law.
The government should identify precisely where current legislation falls short and demonstrate how the proposed bill would address those deficiencies without unnecessarily compromising individual property rights, he said.
"If the problem lies in outdated procedures, inadequate enforcement, weak building maintenance or difficulties coordinating the relevant authorities, why not identify the precise deficiencies and amend the appropriate laws? Who determines fair value?" Chang said.
He questioned how developers' projected profits would be calculated, who would independently verify the assumptions and what safeguards would apply if the actual financial outcome differed significantly from the original projections.
A development's expected profitability depends on factors such as land value, development density, construction costs, financing arrangements and market demand. These projections, he said, should not be confused with an independent assessment of an existing homeowner's property or the value of the replacement unit offered.
If the government intends to adopt a profit-based valuation methodology, it should publish the formula, disclose its assumptions and establish independent verification procedures.
Homeowners should also have a clear avenue to challenge valuations and obtain independent legal advice, particularly when they disagree with a proposed redevelopment.
"A feasibility study is not a completion guarantee. A projected profit is not a financial security. And a promise of a replacement home is not the same as receiving one.
"The government must therefore explain what legally enforceable safeguards would protect affected owners if the developer fails to complete the project.
"These should include appropriate financial security, clear responsibility for temporary accommodation, enforceable completion obligations and a credible mechanism to secure completion if the original developer defaults.
"Without such safeguards, the burden of an unsuccessful commercial venture could fall disproportionately on homeowners who never chose to become participants in that venture," he said.
Chang called for legally enforceable safeguards, including appropriate financial security, clear provisions for temporary accommodation, binding completion requirements and mechanisms to ensure projects can be completed if a developer defaults.
DISTINGUISHING SAFETY FROM COMMERCIAL DEVELOPMENT
Chang said genuinely dilapidated or dangerous buildings may require urgent intervention, but this must be distinguished from redevelopment intended primarily to unlock commercial value.
Local authorities already have powers to address dangerous buildings, while existing maintenance and management laws provide mechanisms to deal with deficiencies in strata properties.
A law intended to improve safety and living conditions should not become a blanket instrument for overcoming the objections of owners who do not wish to surrender their homes, he said.
He also urged the government to examine why existing laws and enforcement mechanisms had not adequately addressed the problems identified before introducing sweeping legislative changes.
Where buildings are unsafe, authorities should enforce existing safety and maintenance provisions. Where management bodies have failed to maintain common property, the underlying causes should be investigated and addressed.
For commercially viable redevelopment projects, developers should negotiate transparently with homeowners and demonstrate that the proposed terms are fair and legally enforceable.
Chang further called for greater scrutiny of proposals that could reduce consent requirements, arguing that majority support for redevelopment should not automatically override the legitimate financial, personal and legal interests of dissenting owners.
Consultation, he said, must give homeowners sufficient information and a meaningful opportunity to raise objections rather than serve as a procedural formality.
"Consultation is meaningful only if homeowners have sufficient information and their objections are properly considered. It should not become a procedural formality before decisions are imposed upon them."
FIX THE EXISTING SYSTEM BEFORE EXPANDING IT
Chang said rather than assuming that a new comprehensive law is the answer, the government should first establish why existing legislation and enforcement mechanisms have failed to address the problems identified.
If the main obstacle is the unanimous-consent requirement for terminating a strata scheme, it should explain why targeted amendments, court-supervised procedures or other narrowly tailored measures would be insufficient.
"Where buildings are unsafe, authorities should enforce existing safety and maintenance provisions. Where management bodies have failed to maintain their buildings, the underlying causes should be investigated and remedied.
"For commercially viable redevelopment, developers should negotiate transparently with property owners and demonstrate that proposed terms are fair, adequately secured and legally enforceable."
Chang said a new law should not be justified simply because it makes redevelopment easier for developers. The government must demonstrate why the changes are necessary in the public interest and how individual property rights will be protected.
He also questioned whose interests urban renewal serves. And why overlook regeneration, revitalisation and rejuvenation as alternative approaches to improving ageing urban areas?
Urban renewal can deliver genuine benefits by improving safety, living conditions and the quality of the urban environment. But these objectives must not come at the expense of homeowners' rights and security.
Chang said developers are entitled to pursue profits, but they must also bear the commercial risks inherent in their business.
Homeowners should not have to surrender their existing homes in exchange for promises contingent on future market conditions, development approvals and a private company's financial survival, he said.
Before proceeding with the proposed legislation, the government must answer two fundamental questions.
"The government must therefore answer two questions before proceeding with the proposed legislation. First, why are existing laws insufficient, and why cannot their shortcomings be addressed through targeted amendments and effective enforcement?
"Second, what concrete and legally enforceable protections will guarantee that homeowners receive fair value and secure replacement properties even if the developer's projected profits fail to materialise?
"Until these questions are answered satisfactorily, projected profits and promises of future replacement properties should not be treated as sufficient assurance for affected homeowners," Chang said.
He said urban renewal must renew the urban environment without diminishing the security of homeownership.
"The law should protect the people whose homes are at stake, not merely facilitate the commercial feasibility of redevelopment."

Title: Boeing narrows nine-month 2026 net loss to US$551mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Boeing's net loss narrowed to RM2.25 billion (US$551 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RM24.38 billion (US$5.98 billion) a year earlier.
Its revenue rose eight per cent to RM289.34 billion (US$70.96 billion) from RM267.10 billion (US$65.51 billion).
Boeing president and chief executive officer Kelly Ortberg said recent aircraft certification milestones and its selection to build the US Navy's next-generation fighter aircraft marked progress for the company.
"Recent milestones, including certification of the B737-7 and B737-10 and selection to design and build the Navy's sixth-generation fighter aircraft, are important steps as we continue building on our progress.
"But we are not done. We remain focused on safety and quality as we redouble our efforts on Lean and disciplined execution to deliver on our commitments and build the durable performance our stakeholders expect," he said in a statement today.
For the third quarter, Boeing's net loss narrowed to US$116 million from US$5.339 billion a year earlier, while revenue increased four per cent to US$24.188 billion from US$23.27 billion.
Its commercial aircraft division recorded a three per cent decline in quarterly revenue to US$10.72 billion from US$11.09 billion, while operating loss narrowed to US$697 million from US$5.35 billion.
Boeing said the division's revenue and negative operating margin of 6.5 per cent primarily reflected a less favourable delivery mix, higher projected costs associated with future production rate adjustments and higher estimated supply chain costs.
The division's operating margin in the third quarter of 2025 was affected by a charge on the B777X programme.
Boeing said the B737 programme continued to progress towards stable production of 47 aircraft a month.
The B737-7 received amended type certification from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration during the quarter, while the B737-10 received certification in October.
Production of the widebody B787 remained stable at eight aircraft a month.
Boeing said the B777X programme continued to progress with B777-9 certification flight testing during the quarter, keeping the first delivery on track for 2027.
The company added that its commercial aircraft division secured 300 net orders, including orders from Turkish Airlines, Ethiopian Airlines and Lufthansa.
It delivered 161 aircraft during the quarter, compared with 160 a year earlier, while its backlog comprised more than 6,300 aircraft valued at a record US$612 billion.
Meanwhile, Boeing's defence, space and security division recorded a 15 per cent increase in quarterly revenue to US$7.935 billion from US$6.902 billion, driven by higher volume.
Operating earnings rose to US$492 million from US$114 million.
The division's operating margin of 6.2 per cent primarily reflected a US$252 million gain from the sale of HRL Laboratories and improved operational performance.
Its backlog reached a record US$101 billion, with 23 per cent of that coming from customers outside the US.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang exco tells ECRL passengers to beware of ticket scams
Article:
KUANTAN: East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) passengers have been told to buy tickets only through authorised channels to avoid scams ahead of sales opening next month.
The ECRL, which will connect Kota Baru to the Gombak Integrated Transport Terminal via Kelantan, Terengganu and Pahang and Selangor, will begin operations on Dec 12.
Pahang Consumer Affairs and Human Resources Committee chairman Sim Chon Siang said scammers might exploit the anticipated demand by offering tickets at unusually low prices, including on social media.
"We understand that many are eager to board the trains, but they should not be duped by individuals taking advantage of the situation. Some may offer discounted tickets to lure buyers, so passengers must remain vigilant.
"The safest way to purchase tickets is through the ECRL's official sales channel once available," he told the
New Straits Times
today.
Pahang has the highest number of ECRL stations at seven, located in Temerloh, Bentong, Maran, Paya Besar, Kota SAS, Kuantan Port City and Cherating.
On Oct 19, the ECRL announced that economy-class fares between Gombak and Kota Baru would start at RM125.
Last week, Transport Minister Anthony Loke announced that all economy-class passengers are set to enjoy a
30 per cent discount
for one month, beginning from the start of operations.
Sim said the public's eagerness to secure seats ahead of the December school holidays could make them vulnerable to scams.
He told passengers to be wary of social media offers promising bulk-ticket discounts, free meals on board or guaranteed seats in exchange for early purchases.
It is learnt that Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd will sell tickets through the project's official website next month, alongside the launch of a mobile application.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Customs foils bid to transit RM49.5mil AI chips through Malaysia, with potential weapons applications [WATCH]
Article:
SEPANG: The Customs Department has foiled an attempt to use Malaysia as a transit point to smuggle advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips worth RM49.5 million to another Asian country.
The attempt was uncovered on Oct 15 when Customs officers seized 30 server units containing advanced AI chips at a warehouse in Kuala Lumpur International Airport's (KLIA) Free Commercial Zone.
KLIA Customs director Aspalila AG Tuah said the servers had been brought into Malaysia from an undisclosed Asian country under a single air waybill and were intended for re-export to another Asian country.
She said the syndicate attempted to evade detection by declaring the servers as ordinary electronic components.
"The syndicate also used Malaysia as a transit point to ensure there would be no restrictions when exporting the servers to their next destination," she told a press conference at the KLIA Customs Cargo Complex.
Aspalila said the seizure was made around 11.30am following an inspection by enforcement officers at a warehouse within the airport's Free Trade Zone.
She said the servers were valued at RM45 million, with estimated taxes of RM4.5 million, bringing the total seizure value to RM49.5 million.
Aspalila revealed that this was the fifth case involving advanced AI chips detected this year, with the combined value of seizures exceeding RM100 million.
She said authorities believed the cases could involve the same syndicate.
The advanced chips are also believed to be capable of being used in technology associated with weapons development.
Aspalila said all 30 servers had been seized for further investigation and inspection, while the freight forwarding company handling the shipment had been called in to assist investigations.
She said preliminary investigations indicated that the servers were suspected of being subject to controls involving unlisted items and restricted activities under the Strategic Trade Act.
Under Strategic Trade Controller Directive No. 1/2025, issued by the Strategic Trade Secretariat of the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry, certain advanced AI chips are subject to notification requirements.
Aspalila said individuals or companies intending to export, transship or transit such chips must notify the secretariat at least 30 days prior if they know or have reasonable grounds to suspect that the chips could be used, wholly or partly, for restricted activities.
Approval must also be obtained before applying for the necessary strategic trade permit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GPS to contest all 82 seats in Sarawak polls – Abang Johari
Article:
KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) will contest all 82 seats in the upcoming 13th Sarawak state election.
Its chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg, who is also Sarawak Premier, said the decision was finalised at a GPS meeting attended by the presidents of all four component parties.
He said the coalition was ready for the election, although the Election Commission (EC) had yet to announce the date.
"We are formally announcing that we will contest the election this year, although we do not yet know the date as it will be decided by the EC.
"GPS is prepared for the election," he told reporters after the meeting at Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) headquarters here today.
On seat allocations among the four component parties, Abang Johari said discussions would take into account the seats won at the previous election.
He said further talks would be held before the coalition finalised its list of candidates.
Asked whether any ministers would step aside from contesting, he confirmed that some would, including leaders from PBB.
"Yes, there are some. Some from PBB will also step aside, but I cannot say who at this stage," he said.
Abang Johari said the candidate list would be finalised before nomination day, with GPS awaiting the EC's announcement of the election dates before deciding on its next steps.
At the 12th Sarawak state election, GPS won 76 of the 82 seats, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) secured four and Pakatan Harapan (PH), through DAP, won two.
The composition of the state assembly subsequently changed after See Chee How left PSB to become an independent assemblyman. Three other former PSB assemblymen – Datuk Seri Wong Soon Koh, Dr Johnical Rayong Ngipa and Baru Bian – later joined Parti Demokratik Progresif (PDP), a GPS component party.
GPS now holds 79 seats, while See remains an independent who supports the government. Together, the government bloc and its aligned representative control 80 of the 82 seats, with DAP holding the remaining two – Padungan and Pending.
PBB currently holds 47 seats, followed by SUPP with 13, PRS with 11 and PDP with eight.
The EC will hold a special meeting here on Nov 6 to determine key dates for the 13th Sarawak election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tun Faisal hits back at Tuan Ibrahim over call for Bersatu to quit PN
Article:
SEREMBAN: Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz has slammed Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man for calling on the party to leave Perikatan Nasional amid the coalition's internal crisis.
Tun Faisal said the crisis stemmed from Pas leaders violating the PN constitution and treating their coalition partner unfairly.
He said Tuan Ibrahim should not support wrongdoing of Pas leaders whose actions violated the law and Islamic teachings.
"What is wrong with Pas? Is its deputy president shielding wrongdoing, injustice and oppression, and practising blind loyalty to his own group?" he said in a statement.
Yesterday, Tuan Ibrahim urged Bersatu to
withdraw from PN
instead of taking steps to weaken the coalition.
Tuan Ibrahim said Bersatu should not seek to dissolve PN while expressing disappointment over the Registrar of Societies' (RoS) decision to deregister the coalition.
Meanwhile, Tun Faisal listed eight "sins" committed by Pas against Bersatu.
In the list, he accused Pas of causing a rift within PN by interfering in Bersatu's internal affairs since February last year.
He also attributed the replacement of the Pas menteri besar in Perlis to weaknesses involving the former state leader and his son.
He said the issue escalated into a dispute involving state Pas leaders and the palace before spilling over into the coalition.
"The former Perlis menteri besar from Pas is related to the Pas president through their children's marriage.
"The Perlis Pas ulama council chief and Pas spiritual leader themselves have stressed that Bersatu was not at fault in this matter," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-Esscom intel chief says he was held in dark room in RM190mil suit
Article:
TAWAU: Former Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esscomm) intelligence chief Senior Assistant Commissioner (R) Datuk Mat Zaki Md Zain claimed he was held in a dark room during detention over a murder investigation.
Mat Zaki claimed the room, known as "Blok Insaf", was commonly used to house prisoners considered disruptive, violent or mentally unwell.
The 11th witness and first plaintiff testified during examination-in-chief by lawyer Sharatha Masyaroh John Ridhwan Lincon in a RM190 million lawsuit against the police and 11 other defendants at the High Court.
The case was heard before judicial commissioner Steve Ritikos.
Mat Zaki also claimed his placement in the block was ordered by PDRM as a form of pre-trial punishment that subjected him to physical, mental and psychological pressure.
However, during cross-examination by Senior Federal Counsel Mardziatun Nisa Ahamadul Kaber, Mat Zaki agreed that the  Prisons Department and police were separate agencies under the Home Ministry, each with different legal powers.
He also agreed with Mardziatun Nisa's suggestion that the policemen named as the first to eighth defendants did not hold the keys, manage the cells or have the authority to determine the schedule for Blok Insaf at Tawau Prison.
Mat Zaki disagreed with the suggestion that prison management, cell control, block assignments and the security of prisoners or detainees at Tawau Prison fell entirely under the authority of the prison director and the Prisons Act 1995.
He also disagreed with the suggestion that separating co-accused charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code into different blocks was a standard security practice by the Prisons Department to prevent collusion or interference with court proceedings.
Asked whether he had contacted any Tawau Prison officer or produced a written instruction from Bukit Aman directing prison authorities to subject him to pre-trial punishment, Mat Zaki said the instruction had been given verbally.
In his witness statement, Mat Zaki claimed the conditions of his detention had affected his health, leaving him with ongoing depression, trauma and severe mental stress. He also said he had been diagnosed with vertigo and required medical treatment and physiotherapy.
The plaintiffs were among eight accused
acquitted and discharged
by the Tawau High Court on Jan 25, 2023, of the murder of e-hailing driver Nurman Bakaratu, 61.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt may use international legal mechanisms to claim compensation for transboundary haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is open to considering suitable international legal mechanisms to seek compensation for transboundary haze.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the option could be explored as the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution currently has no provision for compensation claims between states.
"However, the government is open to examining other legal mechanisms, subject to the basis of international law.
"A comprehensive study of the economic losses caused by haze, including its impact on public health, productivity and economic activity, is important as a basis for policy considerations and further actions," he said.
He was speaking when winding up the 2027 Budget debate for his ministry in the Dewan Rakyat.
On claims that Malaysian companies were involved in forest burning in Indonesia, Arthur said there was no solid evidence to confirm this.
"The ministry, together with the Plantation and Commodities Ministry, is looking into the matter.
"Based on the findings so far, there is no solid evidence confirming that Malaysian plantation companies were responsible for the fires," he said.
Arthur said proposals for financial aid to affected people, particularly gig workers, and for a haze disaster fund also needed further study with the relevant ministries and agencies.
He said the government would continue strengthening enforcement cooperation through bilateral and Asean channels.
"The government's position is clear, anyone proven to have caused pollution will face action under the law.
"At the same time, the government continues to study suitable mechanisms to strengthen the principle of polluter accountability and protect the interests of affected people," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Drug syndicates use luxury condos to evade police
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Drug syndicates are renting luxury condominiums with tight security to hide their operations and evade police.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the properties were used to store drugs before they were moved elsewhere for distribution.
He said the condominiums' strict security arrangements made it harder for police to gain access during raids.
"They target luxury condominiums with multiple layers of security because it makes it difficult for us to penetrate these locations," he told reporters at the city police headquarters here today.
Fadil said the syndicates were prepared to pay higher rental rates for properties offering greater security and privacy.
He said the premises used by the syndicates were rented, while drugs were frequently moved between locations to avoid detection.
"They use these places for storage and keep moving the drugs from one location to another before distributing them to end users," he said.
Fadil said drug distribution methods had also become increasingly varied, with syndicates using both physical communication and online messaging platforms to arrange transactions.
"Among the platforms used were WhatsApp and WeChat, alongside other messaging services and direct communication.
"The drugs were intended for different segments of the market, including customers attending private parties and entertainment outlets," he said.
He said syndicates also distributed liquid MDMA packaged in bottles resembling commercially available beverages.
Fadil said some of the bottled drugs could fetch between RM200 and RM300 each.
He said police believed drugs entering Malaysia from overseas could be processed, stored and repackaged locally before being distributed to customers.
"However, investigations were continuing to establish the supply chains and the involvement of individuals within the syndicates.
"Those involved play different roles, including organising operations, distributing drugs and providing logistical support," he said adding that police were particularly concerned about the involvement of both locals and foreigners in facilitating drug distribution networks.
He said police would continue targeting all levels of the drug trade, including those responsible for storing, distributing and supplying the substances to consumers.

Title: [UPDATED]: Three drug syndicates busted, nearly 394kg of drugs worth RM2.15mil seized
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have crippled three drug distribution syndicates operating in the Klang Valley, seizing nearly 394kg of drugs worth RM2.15 million in nine raids conducted over four days.
The raids, conducted from Oct 19 to 22, targeted locations in Cheras, Brickfields, Dang Wangi and Ampang, Selangor.
City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the operations were carried out by the Kuala Lumpur and Cheras Narcotics Crime Investigation Departments.
He said the raids resulted in the arrest of 23 suspects, comprising 17 locals and six foreigners, aged between 21 and 40.
Fadil said the first operation, conducted between Oct 19 and 21, involved four raids at three condominiums in Sungai Besi, Cheras and Bandar Baru Seri Petaling.
"Ten men were arrested, while police seized 123.574kg of MDMA in 530 plastic packets, 59.05kg of liquid MDMA in 190 bottles and quantities of ketamine.
"The drugs were estimated to be worth RM250,300," he told reporters at the City police headquarters.
In the second operation on Oct 20, police conducted four raids in Sungai Besi, Taman Sri Endah, Ampang Mewah and Bukit Bintang.
"Eleven suspects were arrested.
"The seizures included 52.75kg of MDMA, 130.8kg of liquid MDMA, 9.76kg of MDMA powder, 365g of ecstasy pills, 290g of ketamine, 1,250 Erimin 5 pills weighing 385g and another 5.5kg of liquid MDMA," he said adding that the drugs were valued at RM312,765.
The third operation, carried out at a condominium in Pudu on Oct 22, yielded the most valuable seizure.
"Police seized 10.605kg of MDMA and 1g of methamphetamine, with a combined estimated value of RM1,590,782," he said, adding that the overall drug haul weighed 393.965kg and was valued at RM2,153,847.
"The drugs seized could have supplied an estimated 1.31 million users at any one time, based on an estimated consumption of 0.3g per person."
He said investigations indicated that the syndicates involved individuals performing different roles, including those believed to be leaders, distributors and others responsible for supporting their operations.
Fadil said police were also investigating possible links between those arrested, and did not rule out further arrests.
"We will intensify enforcement against all levels of drug trafficking, from production and storage to distribution and end users," he said urging anyone with information about drug trafficking activities to contact the NCID hotline at 012-208 7222.
